newsitem.title: GREECE: Three dead in Greek storms, heavy damage.
newsitem.headline: Three dead in Greek storms, heavy damage.

text.p: At least three people were killed when storms lashed Greece on Sunday, causing heavy damage, cutting power and sweeping scores of cars through town streets.
One person drowned when a bus was swept up in the flooding near Corinth 85 km (50 miles) west of Athens, public order ministry officials said. Two others died near the western port of Patras.
Extensive damage was reported to hundreds of homes, shops and other buildings around the country. In Corinth, flood waters churned throughout the town and came up to window sills.
Live television reports from Corinth showed scores of empty cars being swept through the streets like toy boats. The streets throughout the town centre were turned into raging rivers.
Electricity was cut in a number of places and telephones were knocked out. A central area of Athens, from Patission to Omonia Square, was without electricity for several hours.
Heavy damage was reported throughout the Peloponnese peninsula, western areas near Larissa and suburbs of Athens.
Rail lines and streets around Athens were heavily floaded and water a metre (several feet) deep churned through suburbs and central intersections.
Athens's fashionable northern suburb of Kifissia was awash, with water lapping against windows of boutiques and shops.
Mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos said the capital had suffered considerable damage but its main problem was a five-day strike by rubbish collectors.
He told a radio interviewer there were now 8,000 tonnes of rubbish in the streets and that the rain had thwarted plans to spray the rotting heeps with disinfectant.
Streams of garbage swept through the streets of Kifissia, piling up along sidewalks and shop windows.
